headline: Tuesday and most of Wednesday stay dry, then a fast-moving cold front brings heavy bursts of rain, gusty winds and possible thunderstorms late Wednesday night into Thursday, with about a quarter to half inch of rain in San Diego County and more to the north.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Tuesday stays mostly dry after Monday night's widespread soaking west of the mountains, with clouds banked up against the mountains and morning clouds along the coast clearing from north to south. Breezy west winds at the coast and valleys ease after about 7 PM. Clouds regather along the coast Tuesday evening, with a 30–40% chance of a low cloud deck at times, mainly between about 2 and 7 AM Wednesday and most likely around San Diego. In the mountains and deserts, gusty southwest winds on the desert slopes begin to ease Tuesday evening.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Wednesday stays dry for most of the day, with temperatures near normal along the coast and below normal farther inland. A strong storm sliding down the West Coast pushes a cold front from northwest to southeast across the region late Wednesday night and Thursday morning; it is strongest in Orange and San Bernardino Counties and weakens as it reaches Riverside and San Diego Counties late Thursday morning or early afternoon, with possible thunderstorms. Rain can fall at 0.25–0.50 inch per hour in San Diego County (heaviest in North County) and 0.50–0.65 inch per hour farther north and in the mountains, enough for street flooding and ponding on roads, along with 30–35 mph gusts at the coast and valleys, so secure outdoor items and watch for falling tree limbs. Totals: 0.25–0.50 inch in San Diego County, 0.50–1 inch in Orange County and parts of the Inland Empire, 0.50–1.50 inches in the San Diego and Riverside mountains, 1–2 inches in the San Bernardino Mountains, 0.10–0.30 inch in the High Desert and 0.10 inch or less in the lower deserts; scattered showers linger Thursday and a weaker disturbance could bring more light rain to northern areas Friday (timing uncertain). In the mountains and deserts, gusts of 50–60 mph hit the San Bernardino Mountains' ridges and desert slopes and 45–55 mph in the High Desert (Wind Advisories late Wednesday night into Thursday), and 40–55 mph in the Riverside and San Diego County mountains and passes, easing Thursday evening; snow levels stay above 7,000 feet during the heaviest rain, then drop to 6,000–6,500 feet Thursday afternoon and evening, with 3–5 inches above 7,500 feet and 1–2 inches below that.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday looks dry, with temperatures staying near to below normal into early next week. Another round of unsettled weather is possible sometime Sunday or Monday, with at least light rain west of the mountains in most computer-model runs. The timing and how far south that storm reaches are still uncertain, with more details expected in the coming days.

coast: A High Surf Advisory runs until 4 AM Wednesday for the Orange County and San Diego County coasts, with surf of 6–9 feet and sets to 11 feet on west-facing beaches, plus strong rip currents through midweek. Surf drops briefly to 3–5 feet with sets to 6 feet on Wednesday, then a new northwest swell raises it again Thursday through Friday. Coastal flooding is expected at times this week because of the high surf, even with tides under 6.5 feet through Friday; King Tides peak next week, with tides over 7 feet possible starting Saturday, Nov. 21. For boaters, a Small Craft Advisory runs until 4 AM Wednesday with 25–30 knot gusts (near gale force around San Clemente Island) and steep 7–10 ft seas, slowly easing Wednesday morning, before steep 7–10 ft seas and 20–30 knot gusts return Thursday into Friday morning.
watch_for: Bursts of heavy rain and 30–35 mph gusts as the front passes Thursday morning and early afternoon, with street flooding possible.
Possible thunderstorms within the front on Thursday.
Coastal flooding at high tide, with King Tides able to top 7 feet starting Saturday.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in dry weather through most of Wednesday and in Thursday's front, less sure about the timing of Friday's light showers, and uncertain about the timing and reach of the Sunday–Monday system.
